_webAuthnPolicyComment: Two-factor WebAuthn policy (security-key-as-second-factor, alongside a password) — used where a flow adds webauthn-authenticator as an additional factor rather than a full passwordless replacement. See identity-security-recommendations.md section 6.
_webAuthnPolicyPasswordlessComment: Passwordless ("passkey") WebAuthn policy — the credential the clinician-browser flow makes MANDATORY (AAL2/AAL3, no password fallback — see identity-security-recommendations.md section 6) and the patient-carer-browser flow offers as the encouraged, phishing-resistant alternative to password+OTP. Keycloak has exactly one policy of each kind per realm, not one per client/role — the assurance-level difference between clinician and patient/carer principals is enforced by which authentication flow requires vs. offers it (see authenticationFlows below), not by two different WebAuthn policies.

clients._directAccessGrantsComment: Enabled ONLY so e2e/ (Playwright golden-path test, added during integration) can fetch a real, correctly-signed token via Resource-Owner-Password-Credentials against services/*.test users below, bypassing the mandatory-WebAuthn browser flow (which Playwright cannot drive without a virtual-authenticator harness this pass didn't build). This is the standard, common way test tooling authenticates against a dev-mode Keycloak realm — the 'browser' flow override below (still mandatory passkey) is completely untouched, so a real user hitting the hosted login page still gets the real, unweakened flow.
clients._authenticationFlowBindingOverridesComme: GP is a clinician principal type — passkey/hardware key is MANDATORY (AAL2/AAL3), not optional. See identity-security-recommendations.md section 6 and modules-and-requirements.md ("Identity & Access").

clients._directAccessGrantsComment: See gp-portal's equivalent comment above — same e2e-only rationale.
clients._authenticationFlowBindingOverridesComme: Specialist is a clinician principal type — same mandatory-passkey rationale as gp-portal above.

clients._directAccessGrantsComment: See gp-portal's equivalent comment above — same e2e-only rationale (patient-web's browser flow only requires password+OTP, so this is a smaller relaxation than the clinician portals', but kept consistent/explicit rather than implicit).
clients._authenticationFlowBindingOverridesComme: Patient/carer principal type — passkey encouraged, password+OTP fallback acceptable (AAL1/AAL2). See identity-security-recommendations.md section 6.

Same patient/carer flow as patient-web above. NOTE (see claude/solution-architecture-tech-stack.md, "Frontend"): native passkey/WebAuthn support through Expo/React Native is flagged there as still maturing — patient-mobile should validate iOS AutoFill / Android Credential Manager passkey support directly before relying on this flow requiring it; password+OTP remains a first-class fallback here specifically because of that risk.

users._clientRolesComment: Grants this service's Keycloak client-credentials service account the realm-management roles it needs to call the Admin REST API on a caller's own behalf (list/revoke WebAuthn credentials, force re-enrolment, list/remove federated identities) — see services/identity-access/src/keycloak-admin/keycloak-admin.service.ts. Deliberately NOT manage-realm or manage-clients — least privilege.

users._e2eTestUserComment: Added during integration/e2e work (e2e/), not part of the original identity-access build — a fixed-password, fixed-role test principal for Playwright's golden-path test to obtain a real token via Resource Owner Password Credentials (see the gp-portal/specialist-portal/patient-web clients' directAccessGrantsEnabled comments above). Never use this pattern/credential outside a local dev realm.
See gp.test above — same e2e-only rationale.
See gp.test above — same e2e-only rationale.

identityProviders._secondaryLinkOnlyComment: linkOnly=true is the actual enforcement mechanism for 'social login is a secondary sign-in method, never a way to create or activate an account' (see claude/solution-architecture-tech-stack.md and claude/modules-and-requirements.md, 'Identity & Access'). With linkOnly set, Keycloak refuses to use this IdP for a fresh login or first-broker-login registration at all — it will not even appear on the login page (hideOnLoginPage) — and can ONLY be reached via the Client Initiated Account Linking endpoint (/realms/{realm}/broker/google/link), which requires an already-valid Keycloak SSO session. services/identity-access/src/account-links is the one place in this platform that constructs that link URL, and it requires a verified bearer token before doing so — see that module for the second, application-layer enforcement of the same constraint. firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias is set as defense-in-depth on top of linkOnly, not instead of it: 'social-linking-only' (below) has no create-new-user branch at all.

Same linkOnly enforcement as google above. Also the practice-tenant SSO path noted in solution-architecture-tech-stack.md ('a lot of AU GP and specialist practices already run Microsoft 365/Entra ID') — still secondary-link-only, never account creation, for the same identity-binding reason.

identityProviders._mockComment: MOCK — replace with real integration. Points at services/identity-access's in-process mock OIDC IdP (src/mock-myid) standing in for myID (TDIF) — see claude/solution-architecture-tech-stack.md, 'Identity and access' ('Keycloak can be configured as an OIDC relying party against a TDIF-accredited identity provider, which is exactly the lightweight path already recommended over seeking TDIF accreditation directly'). Unlike google/microsoft this is NOT linkOnly: identity-security-recommendations.md section 6 frames myID as an optional HIGHER-assurance path (government-grade IP2/IP3 proofing) for elevation to authorised-representative tier or GP/specialist onboarding — a legitimate future account-creation-adjacent use that belongs to the Onboarding & Account Service's flow, not this realm config. It ships disabled (enabled:false) because it isn't wired into any auto-provisioning flow yet — flip to true only once that integration exists. URLs use the docker-compose service hostname (identity-access:3001), matching MOCK_MYID_ISSUER_BASE_URL in services/identity-access/docker-compose.yml env.

authenticationFlows.description: Browser login for patient/carer principals — passkey (WebAuthn passwordless) encouraged, password+OTP fallback acceptable (AAL1/AAL2). See identity-security-recommendations.md section 6 and modules-and-requirements.md ('Identity & Access').

Either a passwordless passkey (preferred) or password+conditional-OTP (fallback) — offered as alternatives, not stacked, matching how passkey login actually works (it replaces the password step, not adds to it).

Browser login for GP/specialist principals — passkey or hardware security key is MANDATORY (AAL2/AAL3), no password/OTP fallback. See identity-security-recommendations.md section 6 ('GPs and specialists ... passkey or hardware security key should be mandatory, not optional') and modules-and-requirements.md ('Identity & Access').

First-broker-login flow for google/microsoft — defense-in-depth alongside linkOnly (see the identityProviders entries above): contains ONLY 'Confirm Link Existing Account', no 'Create User If Unique' branch, so even a future config mistake that flips linkOnly off cannot cause this flow to silently create a new account from a brokered login.

_stepUpAuthenticationComment: Step-up authentication for sensitive actions (revoking a passkey — see services/identity-access/src/passkeys — approving a new GP link, granting deceased-patient access) is READ by services/identity-access/src/common/step-up against the acr/amr claims, but this realm does not yet define the Conditional-OTP/ACR-to-LoA authentication flow that would actually populate a distinguishable elevated acr value after a fresh passkey re-auth — see infra/keycloak/README.md, 'What's NOT in here yet'. Documented here as a known, load-bearing gap rather than silently assumed to work.
_carerVsPatientFlowComment: The carer-vs-patient / OTP account-creation branch (identity-security-recommendations.md section 3) is intentionally NOT modelled as a Keycloak authentication flow — per infra/keycloak/README.md this belongs to the Onboarding & Account Service, which orchestrates it in front of Keycloak (SMS link → DOB/Medicare verify → branch → OTP → Keycloak user creation), not inside a realm's login flow. See that service's own build for its implementation.
